purpose: 90-second narrated demo with Tuen Mun TD detectors and the simulated P2 route

segments.text: When an incident blocks a road, a detour can move congestion somewhere else. Ripple helps traffic operators make that call. Here, its map replays five-minute detector readings from an archived Aberdeen incident. These dots are roadside measurements, not cars or recommended routes.
In Aberdeen, the saved simulation finds no clear winner between targeted advice and doing nothing. Ripple holds back instead of recommending a detour.
The original Transport Department notice remains visible beside the measured speed trend, so the operator can inspect the evidence.

Now Tuen Mun. Coloured dots show roadside detector speeds; white dots mark junctions. The magenta line follows the tested Castle Peak Road detour. Ripple compares no advice, broad advice, and advice to eleven percent of drivers. Across eighteen simulations, targeted advice gives four point three percent less modelled delay; broad advice is worse.
This is a simulation candidate, not a proven road saving. The model queue moves too fast and clears early. A human operator reviews the evidence before any advice reaches drivers.

tuen_mun_observation: The map uses all 27 TD detector locations from sim/tuen-mun/observations_20260415.json and measured speeds from the 18:00 HKT five-minute bin. Count and speed values are not inferred from junction nodes.
route_map_source: sim/scenarios/tuen-mun/evaluator_IN-26-02615_p0x-merge-at-site-s2029.json: plan_actions.routes.Castle Peak Road.with and closure.edge_id; sim/tuen-mun/network.net.xml; network, scenario and observations hashes match the displayed saved P2 run provenance; generated by build_tuen_mun_route_map.py
claims: The Aberdeen verdict is a saved diagnostic. The Tuen Mun 4.3% is the frozen 18-condition modelled comparison; the simulated queue has known physical limitations. The route map shows the tested network edges, not live traffic or an approved road recommendation.
